solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Worthy firm not beyond repair, needing millions invested

indicators.note: money invested is put into something, so the millions are placed within the other pieces

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm
something not beyond repair can still be fixed, so it is mendable
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A business that is struggling but salvageable, if only it can attract big investment, is deemed worthy of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' reads as money put into the firm, which suits the surface, but it simply slots the millions abbreviation in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something deserving praise or approval, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Study poem that's turned up — poet almost intimate

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the poem's title is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: almost means the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A literary scholar reads a poem that has surfaced and finds a poet almost on intimate terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' is Rudyard Kipling's well-known poem; 'turned up' makes FI, and 'almost' trims DANTE to DANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate, used as a noun, is a close friend one trusts with secrets, which is a confidant.

clue.text: Keen fellow harbouring love

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the fellow holds the love within him

parts.note: a fellow is a man
love is nil in tennis scoring, shown by the letter O

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic chap secretly nurses a romantic attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective (eager) but is the verb meaning to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to lament loudly, as mourners do, so it is a synonym of the verb meaning to groan or wail.

clue.text: What enthrals you, short sharp noise from canine

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the interjection holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: eh? is an interjection meaning what?
ye is an old form of you
a toot is a short blast on a horn

explanation.surface: Something that captivates you, a yelp from a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like an adjective meaning doglike, but it is the noun for a pointed tooth. 'What' is the interjection eh?, and 'enthrals' makes it hold the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye tooth is the pointed upper canine tooth, named because it sits beneath the eye.

clue.text: Old coins showing queen maybe, covered in grime mostly

indicators.note: covered in means the animal is wrapped by the dirt around it
mostly means the dirt word loses its last letter

parts.note: dust is dirt or grime
a queen is a female cat, so the animal is an example given by 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Antique coins bearing a monarch's head have been found almost entirely caked in dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' seems to be a monarch on a coin, but it is a female cat. 'mostly' trims DUST to DUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold or silver coins once used across Europe, especially in Venice.

clue.text: Bishop wants someone obsequious, the sort that family might shun

definitions.text: the sort that family might shun

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to want something is to lack it
Uriah Heep is the fawning, 'ever so humble' clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A bishop has no use for a toady, the kind of person his relatives would avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the byword for oily servility in Dickens, so he stands for anyone obsequious.
explanation.definitionFit: A black sheep is the disgraced member a family disowns or keeps quiet about.

clue.text: Chemical dissolving in the steriliser

indicators.note: something dissolving in a liquid disappears into it, so the chemical lies concealed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A chemical is breaking down inside a sterilising unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'thE STERiliser'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic compound formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol, so it is a chemical.

clue.text: US city's generous donor attending first half of gala

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the donor and the next piece stand together

parts.note: Santa Claus is the generous giver of Christmas presents

indicators.note: first half of means only the opening two of the four letters of the gala word are kept

parts.note: a fete is a gala or outdoor festive event

explanation.surface: An American town's big philanthropist turns up for the early part of a charity gala.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gala' gives FETE, and 'first half of' keeps FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital of New Mexico, a city in the United States.

clue.text: This person unfit to hold a political office

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the shuffled letters close around the single letter
unfit means not in proper shape, so the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone deemed unsuitable to occupy an elected post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfit' rearranges THIS PERSON, and 'to hold' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A senatorship is the post of a senator, an elected office in politics.

clue.text: A set of old books with smart binding badly arranged

indicators.note: binding means wrapping round, as a cover binds pages, so the fashionable word encloses the others

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish
OT is the Old Testament, a set of old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Some antique volumes with elegant covers have been shelved in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' looks like a bookbinding term to suit the books, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in disorder, which is what being badly arranged means.

clue.text: Weak PM in the House assumed supine position maybe

parts.note: the House of Commons is a debating chamber
to have lain is to have lain down, supine being one way of lying

explanation.surface: A feeble Prime Minister in Parliament ends up lying flat on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain, British Prime Minister 1937 to 1940, is remembered for appeasing Hitler, hence 'Weak'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain is the British premier widely judged feeble for his appeasement policy before the Second World War.

clue.text: Article protected by nothing secure

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded, so the article sits inside the word for nothing

parts.note: nil means nothing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item left without any protection at all, yet somehow safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secure' is a verb here: to fix firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten it firmly, and figuratively to make it certain, as in nailing a deal.

clue.text: Take hours wandering around old country

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation
wandering means roaming about, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A traveller spends hours strolling through some ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges TAKE HOURS, and 'around' puts them round O.
explanation.definitionFit: South Korea is a nation in East Asia occupying the southern half of the Korean peninsula.

clue.text: Sporty type wears kit specially designed with top person's label

indicators.note: specially designed means freshly made to a new pattern, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher marking items such as postboxes, so it is the Queen's label

explanation.surface: An athlete dons custom-made gear bearing a celebrity's brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially designed' rearranges WEARS KIT; the monarch is the top person, and ER is her monogram.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-skier is someone who takes part in a sport, towed on skis behind a boat.

clue.text: Time to get each person to join social event

parts.note: a party is a person, as in a third party or the guilty party

explanation.surface: It is time for everyone to come along to a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person' gives PARTY in its legal sense, one of the people in a contract or dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is an afternoon gathering where guests meet over tea, so it is a social occasion.

clue.text: Female vocalist leading group not 40, an innocent young thing

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the singer comes before the next piece

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
UB40 is a British reggae band; without the 40 it leaves UB

explanation.surface: A singer fronts a band that has nothing to do with the Top 40 chart, and comes across as naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not 40' looks like a chart position, but it strips the number from the band name UB40.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic child, so the word is used for a sweet, innocent youngster.

clue.text: River rose disastrously — water over a wide area?

indicators.note: disastrously means in ruinous fashion, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The river level climbed catastrophically, flooding the land far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' rearranges RIVER ROSE. The definition reads like a flood, but it describes a large man-made lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large body of stored water spread across a broad expanse, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Office work in which theologian's kept wasting time?

indicators.note: kept means held within, so the clerical task holds the theologian inside

parts.note: filing is routine clerical work in an office
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Clerical drudgery where a religious scholar is kept busy but achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' signals the container; 'in which' only links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddling about means fidgeting or frittering time away, so it is a form of time-wasting.

clue.text: Beast by river is a baddie

indicators.note: by means next to, so the animal stands beside the abbreviation

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: The creature lurking by the water is the villain of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotter is old-fashioned slang for a cad or scoundrel, someone who behaves badly.

clue.text: Line written by one official examiner who grants permission?

definitions.note: stands for 'one who grants permission', a noun

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a censor officially examines books, films or letters

explanation.surface: A line drafted by a single inspector who decides what may be allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty in spirit: it gives I and lets 'who grants permission' read as a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensor issues licences, formally authorising others to do something.

clue.text: Arab island on which the old fellows may sit

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'
fellows are men

explanation.surface: An Arabian isle where elderly men might perch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on which ... may sit' puts the first two pieces above the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a native of Yemen, a country of the Arabian peninsula, so an Arab.

clue.text: Some deaths may be accidental in e.g. farming communities

indicators.note: accidental means happening by chance, so the letters of the two words are rearranged at random

explanation.surface: On farms, some fatalities could be the result of accidents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be accidental' rearranges SOME DEATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Homesteads are farmhouses with their land, the small settlements of an agricultural district.

clue.text: Note car coming from Oxford going on to motorway

indicators.note: going on to means joining, so the car is followed by the road letter

parts.note: the Mini is built at the Cowley plant in Oxford
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Take note: a car from Oxford is joining the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: MINI cars are made at Cowley, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth two crotchets, known in the US as a half note.

clue.text: Zone fare always covers

indicators.note: covers means conceals, so the two words keep the region word out of sight inside them

explanation.surface: A fixed ticket price always applies to a given transport zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'fARE Always'.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district, which is what a zone is.

clue.text: Society that's outwardly flabby and debauched

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the flabby word wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: fat means flabby

explanation.surface: High society, flabby on the outside and morally degenerate within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' puts FAT around S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast is an old word for dissipated or immoral, as in a fast set living a wild life.

clue.text: Writing implements I have in a brown study?

parts.note: pens are tools for writing
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: I keep my pens in a study with brown decor.
explanation.walkthrough: A brown study is an old idiom for deep, absorbed thought, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a brown study means lost in thought, which is exactly the state of being thoughtful and reflective.

clue.text: One desperate fellow outside house, a man in a state?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the comic character goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman cowboy of the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic man waiting outside a house, someone in a real state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests agitation, but here it means living in a US state. Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip character.
explanation.definitionFit: An Idahoan is a resident of Idaho, so a man who lives in an American state.

clue.text: Matron grins doing the rounds — one up bright and early

indicators.note: doing the rounds means circulating, so the letters of the two words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheerful hospital matron on her ward round, smiling as an early riser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the rounds' rearranges MATRON GRINS. The definition sounds like an early riser but describes a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning star is Venus seen shining before sunrise, so it is a bright body up early.
